transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... I have this issue with elevators. I mean, I know they aren't really dangerous, but when I have to get in one, I just get really scared. It's like I feel like I'm going to be trapped in there, and I just can't make myself feel normal about it.
Do you experience similar feelings of fear or anxiety in situations other than being in elevators?
No, not really. It's just elevators. I don't have a problem with small rooms or crowds or anything like that. Just the elevators.
How long have you been experiencing this fear of elevators?
It's been going on for about 11 months now. Um, it started right around the time we lost our house and had to move into an upper-floor apartment.
Is your fear of elevators related to the height of the floors you're traveling between?

No, I don't think so. It's not about being up high. Like I said, it's just the elevator itself that bothers me. I'm fine looking out the window of the apartment or being on the roof at work. It's just getting in that little box to go up and down.
Does your fear of elevators interfere with your daily activities or cause you significant distress?

Yeah, it does a little. I mean, I’m still getting to work and going to my GED classes, so I'm not letting it stop me completely. But... always having to take the stairs makes me late sometimes, and honestly, I'm just worn out before I even start my day. 

And with my construction work, I've actually had to turn down some assignments if the only way up is a site elevator. It just makes me a bit less useful on certain jobs, which is frustrating.
Is it the thought of getting into an elevator that scares you, or does the fear start once you're already inside?

I mean, thinking about it isn't fun, but the real fear hits once I'm actually inside. Like... as soon as those doors start sliding shut, my chest gets tight. My hands start sweating, and all I can think is that I need out of there. It happens right away, even if the job is only going up a few floors.
Is there something specific about the elevator, like a sound or a smell, that triggers your fear?

No, not really. I haven't noticed any specific smell or a certain noise or anything like that. It's really just... the box itself. Just being inside it when the doors shut and knowing I can't just walk out. There's no special sound or anything that sets it off, just the fact that I'm in there.
Is your fear of elevators mostly about not being able to get out if you need to?

I'm not really sure. I haven't really thought about it like that. I mean... I don't think I'm standing there worrying about being trapped or not being able to escape, exactly. It's just... I just feel scared as soon as I'm in one. I don't really know why it happens or what the exact reason is, just that I really don't like being in them.
Do you think your fear of elevators might have something to do with feeling like you're not in control when you're inside one?

I couldn't really tell you. I haven't thought about it being a control thing. I just... I just know I get that scared feeling as soon as I'm in there. I don't really have a good reason for it, plain and simple. I just know I don't like it and I want the ride to be over.
Is your fear of elevators the same for every elevator you encounter, or are there some elevators that scare you less than others?

I haven't really noticed a difference, honestly. I don't take them enough to compare, I guess. If I have to use one, I just get in, feel that same scared feeling, and wait for it to be over. A box is a box to me, so I try to just take the stairs whenever I can.
Did something specific happen to you involving an elevator that might have triggered this fear?

No, not that I can remember. I mean, I've never been stuck in one for hours or had the cables snap or anything crazy like that. I just... I've just never liked them. As far back as I can think of, it's just always been this way. No big event or anything, just a feeling I've always had.
Did something bad or traumatic happen to you around the time your fear of elevators started, about 11 months ago?

No, nothing like that. I mean... even thinking back to about a year ago, everything was just normal. I was just working my regular routine, doing the same stuff on the job site. There wasn't any big accident or... or anything traumatic that happened in my life. So, no, nothing stands out at all.
Do you think your fear of elevators is because you feel like you're not in control of what's happening when you're inside one?

Not really, no. I mean, I don't think it has to do with control. I'm used to being on lifts and equipment on the job site where I'm not the one driving, and that kind of stuff doesn't bother me at all. It's just... I just don't like being inside the elevator itself. It's not about wanting to be in charge of it or anything like that.
Has your fear of elevators stayed the same since it started 11 months ago, or has it gotten better or worse over time?

It's pretty much stayed the exact same. It hasn't gotten any worse, but it definitely hasn't gotten any better, either. Just... steady, I guess. I still get that same feeling every time I have to deal with one.

Do you think you would feel the same level of fear if you were to encounter an elevator in a completely different context, such as a luxury hotel or a modern office building, compared to the ones you usually encounter?

I don't think it would make a difference. An elevator is an elevator, you know? I mean, I haven't really been in any fancy hotels lately to know for sure, but just thinking about it... yeah, I'd probably feel the exact same way. It doesn't really matter how nice the building is.
Do you think your fear of elevators would be less if you were in one with someone you trust?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, most days I just take the stairs at our apartment and on job sites so I don't have to deal with it. If an elevator or a lift is the only way up, I usually either ask for different work, or... well, I'll ride it, but only if somebody I trust is standing right there with me.
Would you say that your fear of elevators is something that you're able to think about and worry about even when you're not actually in or near an elevator?

No, not really. I don't... I don't sit around at home stressing about them or anything. If I'm not at a job site or somewhere where I actually have to use one, it doesn't really cross my mind. It's just when I'm right there and have to figure out a way around it that it bothers me.
If you were in a small, enclosed space that is not an elevator, such as a train car or a small room, would you feel a similar level of fear?
No, I don't think so. It's really just elevators. I ride the train sometimes and I'm fine, and small rooms don't bother me at all. It's just... something about being in an elevator that gets to me.
Would you feel anxious or scared if you were in a very small, enclosed space that is not moving, like a closet or a tiny room?
No, like I said, small rooms don't bother me. A closet or a tiny room would be fine. It's just elevators that give me that feeling.
